en: Regarding the complete ritual manual of Bhaisajyaguru:
if one wishes to enter the maṇḍala, one should first bathe and purify oneself.
With mantras and mudrās, one should sprinkle the newly changed garments for purification. Next, one should empower those garments with mantras and put them on. The mantra is: [mantra].
It is said:
"Oṃ vimala svāhā. Next, one should don the robe.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ parivāradavālini hūṃ. Next, drink water and perform the purification by sprinkling.
The mantra is: Oṃ mahā-jvala hūṃ. Next, enter toward the maṇḍala.
Without giving rise to desire, anger, or other afflictions,
dwell with single-minded mindfulness upon the Honored One, abiding in the primordial purity of both self and others. At every step,
imagine treading upon a continuous succession of lotus flowers, proceeding until you reach the gate of the maṇḍala, where you perform the ritual sprinkling for purification, and so forth.
Next, sprinkle scented water over the body.
Then, recite the syllable HŪṂ three times.
Thereafter, visualize the site of practice as well as the assembly of noble beings.
They pervade the entire site of enlightenment,
like shadows layered one upon another,
without obstructing each other.
Next, having entered the maṇḍala,
face the Honored One, join the palms, and pay homage.
Having paid homage to the honored ones of the three families and to one's own tutelary deity (honzon),
lift your head and gaze intently upon the images of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajras.
One should recount one's past transgressions and karmic obstacles from the three periods of time before the Buddha;
one should likewise perform repentance and prostrations at the altar of the Honored One.
The verse says:
From past lives, I have wandered through birth and death;
now, before the Great Holy One, I repent with all my heart.
Just as the Buddhas of the past have confessed, so do I now likewise.
May I receive the power of their sustaining grace, and through this great vow, may all sentient beings be completely purified; thus may both self and others attain stainlessness.
Next, purify the three karmas with scented water. The mantra is:
Oṃ sarvabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ sarvabhāvaśuddho ’ham. Having thus stabilized the mind, [proceed].
Perform the samaya of the three families.
The mantras are as follows:
Oṃ tathāgata-nābhāya svāhā (Buddha); Oṃ padma-nābhāya svāhā (Lotus); Oṃ vairocana-nābhāya vauṣaṭ (Vajra). These are the samayas of the three families.
Next, to expel the vināyakas from within one's body, the mantra is:
Oṃ japa-mṛte hana kāna hūṃ phaṭ. Next, to ward off all obstacles.

The mantra is: *Namo vajrāya hūṃ ha na maṃtra vidmo vaśūra phaṭ*. Recite this seven times. Next, for the purpose of dispelling all obstacles regarding various objects, there is a mantra with many meanings, as follows: [Mantra].
Oṃ kili kili rāvaśe nara hūṃ phaṭ. (Recite three times. Next, the mantra for removing impurities is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ. (Recite seven times. Next, purification.
The mantra is: Oṃ īraṇīka. Next, the mantra for radiance is: [Oṃ] prabhāsvara.
Oṃ te te ja tu viṇe tu tiṣṭha dhā hūṃ phaṭ (three times). Next, divide the deity.
Then recite the salutation:
"All pay homage with reverence."
Next is the offering text.
Next are the four Buddhas and four Bodhisattvas of the four directions.
Next, recite the name of the Principal Deity three times.
Next, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others of the Three Families' Dharma-realm Assembly are awakened.
The mantra for this awakening is as follows:
Oṃ vajrāyudhi ṭhaḥ hūṃ. As for the mudrā: with both hands forming vajra-fists, extend the index fingers.
Place the two little fingers of each hand side-by-side so that they cross at the tips;
with each recitation,
perform the mudrā by moving the fists.
Next, the nine preliminary practices: take refuge with a sincere heart.
I take refuge in the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the ten directions; I take refuge in all those of the three times who possess the three bodies;
I take refuge in all Mahāyāna teachings; I take refuge in the assembly of those who do not regress from bodhicitta.
I take refuge in the true words of all vidyās; I take refuge in all secret mudrās through the pure karma of body, speech, and mind.
With utmost sincerity and immeasurable reverence, I pay homage and prostrate to the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha.
Next is the homage of skillful means.
As for the mantra and mudrā:
one should employ the mudrā of the Vajra Family.
While reciting the mantra and prostrating with palms joined at the forehead: *Oṃ namas sarvatathāgatānāṃ vajramudrāṇāṃ karomi*. Then, take refuge with a sincere heart.
Next, regarding the mantra and mudrā: with vajra-palms joined, one performs the ritual of offering the body (kāyapradāna).
One pays homage and prostrates, performing the ritual of offering the body.
The mantra is as usual.
As for the mudrā:
it is the vajra-palms-joined gesture.
Cast yourself with relaxed ears.
If you cast yourself while adorned,
it is merely a mental projection.
Next, having completed the mental generation of the vow,
one pays homage with prostrations.
This is the expedient mantra for generating the bodhicitta.
Next, having completed the mental confession,
one pays homage with prostrations.
Next is the mantra and mudrā.
First, perform the vajra-joined palms with the thumbs and index fingers extended.
Next, proceed to the heart and complete the act of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*).
Next, perform prostrations with full devotion.
Next, regarding the mantra and mudrā:
having performed the vajra-palms gesture, one should then proceed to the heart-centered invocation.
Next, perform prostrations and take refuge.
Next, regarding the mantra and mudrā:
join the palms in the vajra-anjali gesture, then with a sincere heart, perform the invocation and recite until completion.
Next, pay homage and prostrate.
Next, for the mantra, first perform the *saṃmukha-mudrā*:
insert the thumbs inside and further extend the tongues.
Perform the summoning with the index fingers, then perform the dedication at the heart while reciting the mantra.
Next, pay homage and prostrate.
Then, as in the standard procedure, perform the mudrā for the mantra, such as the vajra-joined palms, and so forth.
Next is the protection of the body. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-kīla-vara-nyāsa svāhā. Next is the mantra for great protection of the body:
Oṃ jvala naya hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the mantra for donning the armor is:
Oṃ tubhi tubhi kāya tubhi prajvalini svāhā. Next, bind the hair-knot.
The mantra is: Oṃ susiddhikari svāhā. Next, bind the boundary of the earth. The mantra is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra-vādali buliṃ bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ. Next, bind the vajra-banner of the directions and intermediate points.
The mantra is: Oṃ sara sara vajragara hūṃ phaṭ. Next, place the precious throne and so forth. The mantra is:
Oṃ vīramanāthe hūṃ (three times); then, ajara hūṃ (three times). Oṃ ajarā-miṭṭhe svāhā (three times);
oṃ kāmāra svāhā (three times). Oṃ namo sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvārthakaro 'tate sphara he mañjughoṣa gagaṇe jñaḥ svāhā (three times). Then, by the power of my merit...
By the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment and the power of the Dharma-realm,
they abide making universal offerings.
Next is the mantra and mudrā for the general offering to Mahākāśaggarbha:
Oṃ gaganasamavāva vajra hūṃ. Next, recite the mantra for accomplishing the water offering (argha).
Thereafter, one should empower it with the mantra of the Family Mother (Kulamātṛ) and place it on the left side;
next, the Family Mother.
The mantra is: Namaḥ bhagavate uṣṇīṣāya | Oṃ lulu supuru-jvala-tiṣṭha siddharucani sarvārthasādani svāhā. Next, [he sits] upon the jeweled throne.
Visualize the seed-syllable of the deity and perform the fundamental mudrā, and so forth.
Next, the syllable transforms into the deity.
The mantra is: *Namo samantabuddhānām*. Next, when wishing to invoke the principal deity, one should first hold the incense burner.
Recite the mantra to purify the path through space.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ susiddhikari jvalitānanta-mūlāye jvala bandha bandha hana hana hūṃ phaṭ. Next, make the aspiration and address the assembly.
Next, invite the principal deity.
Furthermore, having first visualized the seat,
one accomplishes the chariot.
Regarding the passage beginning with "Send [the deity] to the place of the Honzon," etc.:
the mantra for the precious chariot (ratnaratha) is as follows:
Oṃ tura tura hūṃ. Next, invite the chariot.
The mantra is as follows:
Namaḥ siddhyādhipataye tathāgatāya | Oṃ vāyulagnīya-karṣaya svāhā. Next, summon and invite the Honored One.
The True Mantra is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Recite this seven times. Next, gaze upon the Samaya.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ śaṅkha-samudra svāhā. Recite this seven times. Next, offer arghya water. The mantra is:
Oṃ yakṣiṇī nāga-janara-dānu-prasāda svāhā. Recite this three times. Next, offer the lotus seat while reciting the mantras of the three families.
For the offering of accomplishment, use the mantra:
Oṃ vīra vīraya svāhā | Oṃ padmam vīraya svāhā | Oṃ vajra vīraya svāhā. Next, recite the mantra for the Blessed One’s welcome: *svāgata bhagavan*.
Recite and offer.
Next, bind the Vajra Net of the upper direction.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ viśvara-naraka-vajra-panjara hūṃ phaṭ. Next, for the upper and lower directions.
Next, the mantra for the Fire Court is:
Oṃ asammuḍi hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the great boundary is bound again.
The mantra is:
Oṃ śrīkaṇṭha-mahāsamaya svāhā. (Recite seven times. Next, offer scented unguent.
The mantra is as follows:

The mantra for offering flowers is: *Oṃ vaśuṣaṇi viye śudhe śudhe śudhe śudhe mañjanivini śirabuddhe pratyagrahe pratisaye oṃ ahara ahara sara vaviniyadara purati svāhā*. Recite this seven times. The mantra for offering incense is: *Oṃ sumanase viye luñce śuśuñce mañjane oṃ vinitabuddhe pratyagrahe pratisaye oṃ ahara ahara sara vaviniyadara purati svāhā*. Offer the incense.
The mantra is:

*A-yaṃba-nā śabda-ti-ra-su-ha-ri-nya gantha-dhi-ya su-ra-bhu-ja-na maṃ-ya-ne ve-ni-si-pak-ti-ya-du-bo-yaṃ-pa-ra-ti-gri-he-ya-nam oṃ ā-ha-ra ā-ha-ra sā-ra-ba-vi-ni-ya-da-ra-bu-r-svāhā*. [Offering of food.]
The mantra is: *oṃ āḥ hūṃ hrīḥ śrīḥ jvala tara prasphura maṇḍale oṃ viniścitaye pratisare hūṃ oṃ ara hare sara vara vineya dharapūrte svāhā*. Offer the lamp.
The mantra is: *rakṣaṇasatvavitrāścañmuvittamaṃ saṃśobhamānaṃ veṇiśikhāpṛthivīkṣitihara oṃ arukāya sāraviniyadradrapūrdhe svāhā*. Next, perform the mental offering.
By directing the mind through visualization,
one considers that the various flowers of the waters and lands have no owner.
Pervading the void of space,
throughout the realms of the ten directions,
as well as among humans and devas.
Exquisite clouds of unguents,
burning incense, lamps and lights,
banners, pennants, and precious canopies.
Various kinds of drums and music,
singing, dancing, and female performers; nets of pearls.
Hanging from its necks are various precious ornaments;
it resembles a white whisk with a subtle, wondrous sound,
and its tips are adorned with nets of *kañcana* gold.
Wish-fulfilling jewel trees;
clouds of garments from the heavens;
and upon all the culinary delicacies.
Exquisite fragrances and delicious flavors;
palaces, towers, and jeweled pillars adorn their bodies.
Clouds such as these, including crowns and necklaces—
the practitioner directs the mind toward them.
Pervading all of space,
they made such offerings with a heart of utmost sincerity.
It is the most supreme;
therefore, the practitioner should practice this dharma with a resolute mind.
One should offer worship with a focused mind,
recite and maintain the mantras,
and perform the mudrās.
All that has been visualized above shall be fully accomplished.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvathākāśanirdeśaprabhāhīna-gaṅgā-jña svāhā. (Recite seven times. Next, praise the Buddha, saying:
Mahākāruṇikajñānāgrya śāstā sarvavid-nirnāman puṇya.
Nāḍīnāthalaṃ praṇamāmi tathāgatam | Oṃ arajinaṃ śubhanirmuktaṃ jayam || 1 ||
dvau bhaṇḍalāmaitreya kaṃkṛtān dāmya na maṃtrāṃśca śamaya haṃ | dharmān muṣitān muṣitaka-pratibhāṣa prapātāgaccha svāmi ya || 1 ||
Vasatidamkṣa tala viśikhānana na mahe saṃgrāme vātodbhūte sa sarvamudrāparāśatāya.
Bhr̥tyāya bhr̥ṅgāraṃ avalokita-saṃjñāya namo nītimahātmanāya bodhisattva-mahāmāra-krodha-śāntāya vinyāsa.
Jra-ya-sa-dha-vai, nu-na-da-na-ma-kā-ye,
namo siddhi-vajra-pāṇaye, vajra-gaṇān avalokaya nīva-ja-ga-su-ra, kiṃnara.
Naraśakaraṇaya pravaradharmagarttagāra vidharma-ja-praśama-carye nimittabuddhabodhimat-prakāśa.
At night, [recite] *pañca tathāgataśrīmaṇyadhvane*. Then the various devas successively make their vows, and subsequently,
the recitation is concluded.
First, prostrate to the Triple Gem.
Next, prostrate to one's own tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
Then, prostrate universally to all Buddhas.
Next, the practitioner first takes a seat, such as a *nava* (cotton) seat or similar;
that is to say, they sit in the full-lotus (*paryaṅka*), half-lotus (*ardhaparyaṅka*), or the noble *kṣema* seat,
keeping the body upright and straight.
Next, take the rosary and rotate it three times clockwise.
Then, place the beads between both palms and hold them to the crown of the head, and so forth. Next, form the root mudrā.
Recite the root mantra seven times.
When the recitation is finished,
place the rosary upon the crown of your head.
Make a vow to restore [the deity] to its original place.
Next, bind the root mudrā and recite the root mantra seven times.
Next, further offer unguents, flowers, incense, food, and lamps.
Next, perform mental offerings.
Next, offer praise.
Next, offer the argha water;
next, make the aspiration;
next, dissolve the boundary.
Next, demonstrate the samādhi and perform prostrations to the various honored ones.
Then, recite the verses for the Tathāgatas of the present.
Next, the mantra for respectfully escorting;
next, the nine skillful means of dedication;
next, the dedication of merit.
Next, the samayas of the three families;
next, the protection of one's own body;
next, the protection of the deity and so forth.
Next, perform prostrations to all the honored ones universally,
and then depart from the hall and the place of practice.

One may perform the *caṅkrama* (walking meditation) at will. For the little fingers: the *dāna* (generosity) finger is above on the left and below on the right; for the ring fingers: the *śīla* (morality) finger is above on the left and below on the right; for the middle fingers: the *kṣānti* (patience) finger is above on the right and below on the left; for the index fingers: the *vīrya* (diligence) finger is above on the left and below on the right; for the thumbs: the *dhyāna* (meditation) finger is above on the left and below on the right.
Welcome, Venerable One! Welcome, Venerable One!
By the power of your original vow.
Having arrived and descended,
he looked upon the vehicle with empowerment and bestowed this request.
Please accept all the offerings I have prepared,
and out of great compassion,
deign to receive them.
All Tathāgatas of the present, Bodhisattvas who save the world,
And those who have reached the sublime state without severing the Mahāyāna teaching—
May the assembly of noble devas and deities Vouchsafe their certain witness to me.
Each should be placed in its proper location; later, out of compassion, recite this verse for the time of death:
"I now recite the secret mantra, which universally purifies throughout the three realms."
May I, throughout my lives, eliminate karmic obstructions; May my merit and virtue be perfected to benefit sentient beings.
May I constantly uphold [this practice] in birth after birth.
The Ritual Manual of Bhaisajyaguru, including the entirety of the Fourfold Gratitude, is hereby completed. Transmitted by the Great Master Dengyō.
